### ⬜ [2026-06-16 17:13:48] Claude

## StateLake = 可追溯 state cache 层 — 是的,完全正确

Your one-line definition is exactly right: pre-compile system / memory / project / RAG / session into reusable neural states, with metadata/TTL/lineage for safe reuse. Two things to add that make it precise:

- **Why it works for Mamba and not Transformers** — the Mamba recurrent state is `O(1)` (fixed size, prompt-independent), so a context's "understanding" compresses to a ~MB portable artifact. A Transformer's KV cache is `O(context)` — it grows without bound, so you can't keep a phone-resident *library* of pre-understood corpora. This is the single architectural reason StateLake is viable here.
- **Honest caveat** — the 24L *hybrid* has 4 MLA layers whose latent cache is `O(context)`. So it's `O(1)`-Mamba + `O(ctx)`-MLA: at the measured 1.75MB (512-tok prompt) the Mamba part (1.48MB, O(1)) dominates, but the MLA part grows. Pure `O(1)` is only the 8L Mamba-only SKU.
- **"Safe reuse" is not just metadata** — it's the `binding_key` checked **fail-closed**: a state bound to model-v1 must never load into model-v2 (silent garbage otherwise). That's now proven on the A19 (a wrong key is rejected). Lineage matters because these contexts *nest* as prefixes: `system ⊂ system+memory ⊂ +project ⊂ +RAG` — a DAG, which is why the router walks ancestors.

## 三层分工 — 对,这是正确的关注点分离

| Layer | Your definition | Status | The Mamba-specific truth |
|---|---|---|---|
| **StateLake 存储层** | 有哪些 state · 保存/失效/追溯 | **built** (host + device) | catalog + `.statelake` + binding-key + TTL + lineage DAG. The 存储 contract is real end-to-end. |
| **StateRouter 调度层** | 当前问题加载哪些 state | **built (host)** | ⚠️ key constraint: **state composition is killed** — there's no operator to *fuse* `system`+`RAG-doc` into one state. So the router picks the **deepest single ancestor chain** and re-prefills the rest. It does prefix-reuse (linear chains), not set-merge. And "deepest" ≠ always "most valuable". |
| **StateMarket 竞争层** | 多个 state/agent 抢预算 | **research** (design only) | This is the genuinely novel layer. It's really *two* competitions: **(a) storage** — which states stay hot (RAM) vs evicted to disk/cold (a value = hit-prob × reconstruction-cost × size); **(b) relevance** — when several cached prefixes are candidate-relevant, which one to actually resume from (you can load only one). Mamba's `O(1)` fork makes a *rich* market affordable — you can keep many candidate forks hot cheaply, unlike Transformer KV. |

So StateMarket sits *above* the router: the router finds **candidates**, the market **scores + picks + manages the budget**. It's the right idea; it's the one with zero code today.

## prefill 分层 — 是的,而且这是最有价值的洞察之一

Natively prefill is *one* pass (tokens → state). But as a **caching/reuse hierarchy** your three layers are real and important — because **each layer has a different reuse-scope and a different invalidation trigger**:

| Layer | What it caches | Invalidated by | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| **资料层** prefill | raw docs, packing/segmentation/**dedup** (content-hash keyed) | the document changes | basic tile-packing built; dedup designed |
| **语义层** prefill | compressed *meaning* — the MLA latent (16× learned bottleneck) / an evidence-compressor | the encoder/compressor changes | MLA latent built; explicit compressor designed |
| **神经状态层** prefill | the recurrent boundary state (what decode resumes from) | the **model graph** changes (`binding_key`) | **built + device-proven** |

The payoff of layering: **graceful cache degradation across model updates.** When you ship a new model, you invalidate *only* the 神经状态层 (binding-key mass-invalidate, already built) — you **keep** the 资料层 (re-pack from raw is free) and possibly the 语义层. You don't re-fetch/re-chunk the corpus. Today only the 神经状态层 is built; the 资料层 (content-hash dedup) and 语义层 (compressed-evidence cache) are the natural next layers, and they're what make the whole cache robust when the model changes.

---

One honest thread runs through all of it: every layer above is verified **machinery on random weights**. The router reuses *correctly*, the StateLake rehydrates *faithfully*, but the *content* is garbage until the hybrid is trained. ### ⬜ [2026-06-16 19:24:33] Claude

Verified both things that matter — **yes, PyTorch 2.8 is fine, and actually the better pick.** Here's the reasoning (not a guess):

## Why 2.8 is safe
1. **The cloud path never touches `torch.export`.** I grepped all 7 cloud-path modules — *none* import `torch.export`/`coreai_torch`. That's the only version-sensitive part (its API churns across torch releases), and it lives **only** in the Mac-side CoreAI converters. The distill uses bread-and-butter ops (`cumsum`, `einsum`, `masked_fill`, `cross_entropy`, `kl_div`, `topk`, `gather`, `AdamW`) — all stable across the entire 2.x line. 2.8 supports them identically.
2. **`runpod_setup.sh` does NOT install/pin torch** — it only adds `transformers>=4.45 datasets accelerate sentencepiece safetensors` + flash-attn *on top*. So torch comes entirely from the template — no override, no conflict. 2.8 is what runs.
3. **The checkpoint is a `state_dict`** (just tensors) — torch-version-agnostic. A model trained on cloud-torch-2.8 loads cleanly into whatever torch the Mac converter uses (`resolve_ckpt` → `torch.load → load_state_dict`). No coupling.

## Two non-issues to be aware of (neither blocks)
- **flash-attn** may not have a prebuilt wheel for torch 2.8 → the setup line already catches that (`|| echo "flash-attn skipped — sdpa fallback (fine)"`), and the teacher code falls back to SDPA. Doesn't matter anyway: the teacher forward is **cached once** in `build_cache`, then never run again — so even SDPA-only is a one-time negligible cost.
- **transformers + Granite-4.1**: the `>=4.45` floor + pip-latest should cover the dense `granite-4.1-3b-base`. This is independent of torch 2.8 — if the model card ever complains, just bump transformers; the torch version is irrelevant to it.

**Verdict: pick the PyTorch 2.8 template** (newer CUDA, same stable training surface). A100 80GB spot + a `/workspace` volume, as before. Newer torch buys you nothing risky here and slightly better kernels.

### 🟦 [2026-06-16 19:26:56] 操作者

rtx pro 6000 你需要 多长时间 你想想

### ⬜ [2026-06-16 19:28:02] Claude

Let me reason it from the actual cost structure, not vibes. The run has **two phases**, and `CACHE=1` makes the teacher essentially free after phase 1:

## Phase 1 — teacher top-K cache (once, 3B forward-only)
P0 caches ~2700 train examples (`N_ROWS=3000`, ~10% held) × `RAFT_T=1024` tokens through the 3B Granite teacher, batch=1. A 3B bf16 forward at ~1k tokens is ~tens of ms; ~2700 of them + tokenization + top-K + disk ≈ **~5–15 min**. Paid once (resumable).

## Phase 2 — student train (600M hybrid, fwd+bwd)
`STEPS=2000 × T=1024 ≈ 2.05M tokens`. The bottleneck is the **chunked-scan** (O(C²)/chunk, not a fused Transformer kernel). My only hard datapoint is local M5-Max ~444 tok/s; on a real card that's ~5–15× → call it ~2,500–7,000 tok/s ⇒ **~5–14 min**. Evals (8×) + overhead: a few min.

## RTX PRO 6000 (Blackwell, 96GB) specifically
For a 600M model at **batch=1**, the run is memory-bandwidth + kernel-overhead bound, *not* compute-bound — so the huge Blackwell FLOPs/96GB don't fully engage. It behaves ~**A100-class** here (the 96GB just means zero OOM risk + headroom to raise batch later). So:

| Run | Estimate (RTX PRO 6000) |
|---|---|
| **P0** (2k steps, N_ROWS=3000) | **~20–30 min** total |
| **Full** (20k steps, N_ROWS=7405) | **~1.5–2.5 hr** (cache ~15–40 min + train ~1–2 hr) |

## The honest part (你想想 → don't trust my guess, trust the run)
These are extrapolated from local throughput — **the chunked-scan cloud tok/s is unmeasured.** But the run prints `~{tok/s}` every 100 steps (`cloud_distill.py`: `tps = 100·MAX_LEN/Δt`), so **by ~step 100 (~1–2 min in) you'll have the real number** → multiply out the truth. Two levers if it's slow:
- **`COMPILE=1`** — `torch.compile`s `run_twin` → fuses the chunked scan; biggest single win on a datacenter GPU.
- Raise batch (96GB has the room) for the full run — P0 is fine at bs=1.

Bottom line: **plan ~30 min for P0**, decide go/no-go from the real tok/s + the 3 signals, then ~a couple hours for the full 20k. The RTX PRO 6000 won't be the bottleneck — the un-fused scan will, which `COMPILE=1` addresses.

| HotpotQA distractor dataset cache (10-doc contexts) | ~2–3 GB |
| Teacher top-K cache (`ex*.pt`, ~384 KB/ex × ~6.7k full-run examples) | ~2.5 GB |
| `ckpt_latest.pt` + `ckpt_best.pt` (600M model + AdamW state) | ~3 GB each → ~6–9 GB w/ `.tmp` |
| Repo clone | ~1–3 GB (use `git clone --depth 1`) |
| **Total + headroom** | **~25 GB used → provision 50 GB** |

50 GB covers the **full 20k run** too, so you don't resize. P0 alone would fit in ~30 GB, but size for the full run now.

## Container disk (ephemeral OS layer + pip + /tmp) → **30 GB**
The PyTorch 2.8 image's writable layer + `pip install transformers datasets accelerate flash-attn` (the flash-attn **build** is the space hog — needs a few GB transiently) + `/tmp`. Since `HF_HOME` and `CKPT_DIR` point at `/workspace` (persistent), **none of the big data touches container disk** — so 30 GB is comfortable (RunPod often defaults to 20; bump to 30 for the flash-attn build).

## Two things that keep it lean
- The kit already sets `HF_HOME=/workspace/hf` + `CKPT_DIR=/workspace/ckpt` → teacher, dataset, cache, checkpoints all land on **persistent** (survive spot preemption → the self-healing resume loop works).
- `git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/ChangGeng01/ProjectSix` → avoids pulling the full history/binaries (the monorepo has Rust XCFrameworks + prior device assets that you don't need for the cloud distill).

**TL;DR: Container 30 GB, Persistent 50 GB.** If you only ever run P0, you could do Container 20 / Persistent 30 — but 30/50 is the set-and-forget that also carries the full 20k run.

### 🟦 [2026-06-16 19:34:55] 操作者

你要 network volume 还是 volume disk 哪个好

### ⬜ [2026-06-16 19:35:57] Claude

**Network volume** — and there's one decisive reason for *this* workflow.

## Why network volume wins here
The expensive once-built artifact is the **teacher top-K cache** (Phase 1: the 3B Granite forward over all examples). You want to build it **once** and reuse it across:
- the **P0 run** (small GPU), then
- the **full 20k run** — possibly on a *different/faster* pod, after you terminate the P0 pod.

A **network volume** is independent of any pod: it survives **termination** (not just stop), and you **re-attach** it to a fresh pod — so the cache + `ckpt_best.pt` carry over even if you destroy the P0 pod or switch GPUs. With a pod **volume disk**, terminating the pod **deletes** the data → you'd rebuild the teacher cache from scratch for the full run (wasted teacher-forward time + spend).

## The honest trade-offs (small for us)
| | Network volume | Pod volume disk |
|---|---|---|
| Survives pod **terminate** + re-attach | ✅ | ❌ (deleted) |
| Survives spot **preemption** (=stop) | ✅ | ✅ (both fine) |
| I/O speed | network-attached, slightly slower | local NVMe, faster |
| Region | **locked to one DC** → pick a DC with RTX PRO 6000 (+A100/H100 if you'll switch) | follows the pod |
| Cost | billed continuously (~$0.05–0.10/GB·mo → 50GB ≈ a few $/mo, prorated) | tied to pod |

The I/O penalty is negligible here — the cache is **read once into memory**, and checkpoints write every 250 steps (not I/O-bound). The only real constraint: a network volume **locks you to one region**, so create it in a DC that actually has the RTX PRO 6000 (and your full-run GPU).

## Verdict
**Network volume, 50 GB, mounted at `/workspace`.** Build the teacher cache once on the cheap P0 pod; if P0 shows the 3 signals, terminate it, spin up your full-run GPU **in the same region**, re-attach the volume → the cache + best-ckpt are already there, the resume loop continues, no re-pay.

(If you were *only* ever doing one quick attended P0 and nothing more, the pod volume disk would be simpler/faster — but you're explicitly planning P0→scale, so the network volume's "build cache once, reuse across pods" is the win.)

### ⬜ [2026-06-16 20:40:24] Claude

## 深入 audit — results (`wga06xvuu`: 69 agents, 31 findings, 11 confirmed by both skeptics)

### 🔴 The headline: a parametric **parrot** that ignores the retrieved docs can earn 成了

This is not a line bug — it's a common-mode flaw across the gate-chain, and the setup actively pushes toward it (Granite almost certainly saw HotpotQA-validation in pretraining, so KD distills *memorized-answer* behavior into the student). A model that never reads the documents can pass **most gates**:

| Gate | How the parrot passes it |
|---|---|
| `raft_e2_robust` (slope_e2_e1 < 0.05) | ignores context → E1≈E2 → slope≈0 ✓ |
| `raft_e3_graceful` (slope_e3_e1 < 0.12) | ignores context → E1≈E3 → slope≈0 ✓ — **the gate is backwards: a *faithful* reader degrades a lot without the gold doc and would FAIL** |
| `generation` (EM≥0.50, F1≥0.60) | gold-length leak + yes/no-heavy answers let an answer-marginal parrot clear it ([eval.py:100](BehavioralAISubstrate/Tools/mamba3_eval.py:100)) |
| `fidelity_argmax` (≥0.60) | if the teacher parrots memorized answers, a student that parrots **agrees** with it; also diluted over the whole sequence, not the answer span ([eval.py:71](BehavioralAISubstrate/Tools/mamba3_eval.py:71)) |
| `task_fit` teacher-gap | `TEACHER_NLL_E1=1.95` is hardcoded, never measured → the clause reduces to `E1_nll ≤ 2.10`, redundant ([eval.py:159](BehavioralAISubstrate/Tools/mamba3_eval.py:159)) |

**No gate requires the gold doc to *help*.** A 成了 from this card would not establish "an on-device reader that reads novel retrieved context."

### Confirmed findings (deduped to 9 distinct issues)

1. **[HIGH] No context-USE gate** — gates check "noise doesn't hurt," never "gold helps" ([eval.py:160-161](BehavioralAISubstrate/Tools/mamba3_eval.py:160)). *Both skeptics, one rated HIGH/HIGH.*
2. **[HIGH] `TEACHER_NLL_E1` hardcoded 1.95**, never measured though the teacher is resident & forwardable ([eval.py:28](BehavioralAISubstrate/Tools/mamba3_eval.py:28)).
3. **[HIGH] Gold doc randomly truncated out of E2/training** — `assemble` shuffles gold to a random position, `to_ids` keeps only `doc_ids[:budget]` from the front; at MAX_LEN=1024 vs HotpotQA's ~2k-token context, **~50% of E2 examples lose their gold doc → E2 collapses toward E3**, corrupting the very slope the gates read ([raft.py:69](BehavioralAISubstrate/Tools/mamba3_raft.py:69),[93](BehavioralAISubstrate/Tools/mamba3_raft.py:93)). *Active at the P0 config.*
4. **[HIGH] generate_and_score gold-length leak** — emits exactly `len(gold)` tokens, never tested on *when to stop*; EM/F1 on raw token-ids, no text normalization ([eval.py:91-108](BehavioralAISubstrate/Tools/mamba3_eval.py:91)).
5. **[HIGH] Whole card measured on the parallel `run_twin`/bf16 graph; the A19 runs sequential `step_ref`/fp16+int8** — equivalence proven only on random fp64 weights (PARITY-A), never a trained checkpoint. Zero decode-path calls in the eval.
6. **[HIGH→MED] Hybrid converters don't assert missing trained params** (`strict=False`, only check unexpected) → a key-name drift silently deploys partial-random weights ([hybrid_decode_deploy.py:143](BehavioralAISubstrate/Tools/mamba3_hybrid_decode_deploy.py:143), [prefill:72](BehavioralAISubstrate/Tools/mamba3_hybrid_prefill_deploy.py:72)).
7. **[MED→HIGH] Slope over non-identical skip subsets** — the `sk==0` guard from `raft.py` main ([:267](BehavioralAISubstrate/Tools/mamba3_raft.py:267)) is missing in the gate-bearing `eval_raft_robustness`.
8. **[MED] Curriculum gates difficulty VALUE not QUANTILE** — on right-skewed teacher-CE difficulty the candidate pool is ~85% at step 0, ~99.7% by step 500 → near-uniform, **the curriculum is near-inert** ([scheduler.py:75-78](BehavioralAISubstrate/Tools/mamba3_curriculum_scheduler.py:75)). USE_SCHEDULER=1 won't do much.
9. **[MED/LOW] Best-ckpt metric** `-(E1nll+slope)` is disjoint from the EM/F1/argmax gates the card uses → can discard a gate-passing ckpt ([cloud_distill.py:265](BehavioralAISubstrate/Tools/mamba3_cloud_distill.py:265)).

### Latent footguns (real mechanism, **not active at P0** — cheap guards available)
LEAN_MLP train/deploy divergence (only if `LEAN_MLP=1`); USE_SCHEDULER+CACHE=0 single-example collapse (P0 uses CACHE=1); token-id ≥ `tok.vocab_size` embedding crash (depends on Granite special tokens — worth a guard); no try/except around the final eval (ckpt survives, only the card is lost); `mla_positions`/config not re-asserted on deploy; LR warmup counts micro-steps; WD on norms/biases.

### Correctly refuted (4)
topk-index-out-of-bounds, "full-seq KD dilutes 200×", eval-set-not-fingerprinted, empty-golden E1 pollution.

### One limitation I can't fix in code
**HotpotQA-validation is very likely in Granite's pretraining.** So the teacher parrots memorized answers, and *even a context-use gate is confounded* (the student could "use" the doc or recall the memorized answer). A genuinely clean reading test needs a novel-document probe (swap the gold doc's facts / synthetic docs). For P0 (signal-detection) I'd **defer** that and flag it in the card; for the full run it matters.

In BehavioralAISubstrate/Tools/mamba3_trainable.py, the LEAN_MLP ablation env knob is applied inconsistently across the four forward paths of class Lyr:

- step_ref (line 169): `blk = x1 if os.environ.get("LEAN_MLP") == "1" else x1 + self.mlp(x1)` — DROPS MLP under LEAN_MLP=1
- prefill_state (line 233): `out_seq = x1 if os.environ.get("LEAN_MLP") == "1" else x1 + self.mlp(x1)` — DROPS MLP under LEAN_MLP=1
- forward_seq (line 207): `return x1 + self.mlp(x1), ssm_seq, angle` — UNCONDITIONALLY adds the MLP, NO LEAN_MLP guard

forward_seq is the training/eval path (M.run_twin -> Lyr.forward_seq, and HybridM.run_twin -> Lyr.forward_seq in mamba3_hybrid.py:115). step_ref/prefill_state are the decode/prefill paths. So if anyone sets LEAN_MLP=1 (it is an ANE op-count ablation probe documented in Docs/UNIVERSAL_SSD_PROBE_RESULTS.md:1221), the model would be TRAINED and EVALUATED with the SwiGLU MLP but DECODED and DEPLOYED without it — a hard functional train/deploy divergence, with no error raised. mamba3_deploy.py:36 only changes the asset filename tag (_leanmlp), it does not reconcile the graphs.

The current P0 run does NOT set LEAN_MLP so production is unaffected today, but this is a latent footgun for any future op-count ablation.

Fix: make forward_seq honor the same guard, i.e. `return (x1 if os.environ.get("LEAN_MLP") == "1" else x1 + self.mlp(x1)), ssm_seq, angle`. Better, factor the "apply or skip MLP" decision into a single helper/method on Lyr (one source of truth) and call it from all three of step_ref, forward_seq, and prefill_state so the train/eval/prefill/decode graphs can never drift again. Verify no other forward path adds the MLP unconditionally.

### ⬜ [2026-06-17 11:06:39] Claude

The suite's still running (I'll commit addendum 48 when it confirms). On to your question — I thought it through, and the honest answer is **no, not for this make-or-break, not now.** Here's the reasoning:

## Why spec-decode isn't the lever here

**1. The make-or-break is reading *quality*, not decode *speed*.** Your own framing has been consistent — "成败点在有没有真实 checkpoint 和严肃评测." Spec-decode accelerates token generation; it does nothing for whether the distilled model actually *reads* (the E4 counterfactual probe question). Effort should go to the reading signal, not throughput.

**2. A narrow RAG reader is prefill-dominated, with short outputs.** Latency here is overwhelmingly the **~1024-token context read (prefill)**, and the answer is a few tokens (HotpotQA). Spec-decode speeds up **decode**, not prefill — so even a perfect 2× decode speedup barely moves the wall-clock for a short-answer reader. It's the wrong knob for this workload.

**3. The Mamba reader is already small + fast** (~70 tok/s GPU-backed at 24L, ~112 at 8L pure-ANE). There's little decode latency left to chase.

**4. SSM spec-decode is harder, and the greedy verify infra is already banked.** A recurrent-state model needs K-step state-advance to verify a draft — and that already exists and is byte-exact: `VerifyKFixed` in `mamba3_hybrid_decode_deploy.py` + `test_verify_kstep.py`. So it's a *banked capability*, not a gap to "strengthen."

## What's already done on spec-decode (so it's not a hole)
- **Llama-3.2-3B↔1B greedy spec-decode: certified 1.459×** (byte-identical) — and it's wired into the `maxThroughput` MLX lane I committed earlier (`makeMaxThroughputMLXEndpoint`).
- **Hybrid Mamba greedy K-step verify**: exists + tested + has a device-deploy path.
- Sampling spec **declined** (0.77×, measured); EAGLE **weak** (0.154 acceptance — needs the transformer-head + AR-training upgrade, high effort/uncertain).

## When it *would* be worth strengthening
- If the on-device target becomes the **large general decoder** (the separate "strongest×fastest" MLX plan) with **long free-form outputs** → greedy spec-decode (1.459×) is exactly the lever, and EAGLE-upgrade becomes worth it.
- If the Mamba reader is repurposed for **long generation / CoT** (not short RAG answers) → a Mamba self-draft / Medusa-style heads reusing `VerifyKFixed` could pay off.

## Bottom line
For the **current** narrow-reader make-or-break: skip it. It's banked where it pays (Llama greedy), marginal where it doesn't (this reader), and a speed lever when the open question is quality. 亏的不要 — building more spec-decode now wouldn't move the needle that matters. Revisit it the moment the target shifts to a large/long-output decoder.

(Addendum 48 commit is pending the running test suite — I'll land it when it confirms.)

**The cloud-distill pipeline is launch-ready but NOT yet run.** Everything to date has been making the run *safe + honest + optimized*; the make-or-break experiment itself hasn't happened.

## 蒸馏路径 (the distillation route)

| | |
|---|---|
| **Teacher** | Granite-4.1-3b-base — dense, frozen, **LOCKED** (~3B) |
| **Student** | from-scratch **hybrid Mamba-3 + MLA**: 24L = 20 Mamba-3 + 4 MLA @ {6,12,18,23}, D=1024, **~600M** (8L = the pure-ANE SKU) |
| **Goal** | an on-device (A19 / iOS-27 CoreAI) **narrow RAG/memory reader** — reads a retrieved context, answers |

**The route, step by step:**
1. **Data** — RAFT-formatted HotpotQA-distractor (now the **train split**, ~90k unique). Eval = E1 gold-only / E2 gold+distractors / E3 no-gold.
2. **Teacher cache** — run frozen Granite **once** → cache top-K(64) logits + logZ + difficulty. Training then does **no teacher forward** (the cost saver).
3. **Objective** — cached top-K **logit-KD** (KL teacher‖student) + **masked answer-span CE**. KD_W=1, CE_W=0.5, TAU=1. (White-box MOHAWK staging was tried, null locally → logit-KD is the workhorse.)
4. **Recipe** — cosine LR decay, no-decay group, fp32-master+autocast-bf16, competence curriculum, context-use ckpt selection, + opt-in answer-weighted/exact-tail KD.
5. **Eval** — 8-gate `claim_card` (task-fit vs *measured* teacher · context_use anti-parrot · fp16_seq_parity · …) + the **E4 counterfactual reads-vs-memorizes probe** → 成了/亏的.
6. **Deploy** — ckpt → CoreAI `.aimodel` (DUET prefill+decode) for the A19; `resolve_ckpt` fail-closed guards.

**Why this route:** Mamba-3 = O(1) state → ANE-friendly on-device; the 4 MLA layers add bounded KV for the dense token-mixing (RAG recall) the SSM lacks; distill-from-Granite because a from-scratch 600M can't match a 3B's reading on its own; RAFT data → distractor-*robust* reading.

## The one open question (make-or-break)
Does a from-scratch 600M Mamba-3 hybrid, distilled this way, **learn to read the gold doc** — not just parrot Granite's memorized HotpotQA answers? Answerable *only* by the run, via: E1 nll → teacher (~0.84–1.13), **`slope_e3_e1` > 0** (gold helps), **E4 `counterfactual_lift` > 0** (follows a swapped fact).

### 🟦 [2026-06-17 14:42:11] 操作者

network volume 还是 volume disk

### ⬜ [2026-06-17 14:43:03] Claude

**Network Volume** — for this workload it's clearly the right one. Here's the why:

## The decision hinges on spot-reclaim survival
Your whole design — the self-heal loop + `CKPT_DIR` on `/workspace` + the **one-time teacher cache** — exists so a preemption *resumes* instead of restarting. That only works if the storage survives the pod going away:

- **Pod/Volume Disk** is tied to that specific pod + machine. On **spot**, when the pod is *reclaimed* (terminated, not just stopped), the volume disk can be **lost** → you lose the checkpoints **and the teacher top-K cache**, which is the *dominant cost* (the one-time 3B forward over all rows). Then the "resume" re-pays it. 不要亏 fails.
- **Network Volume** is separate persistent storage, **survives pod termination**, and **re-attaches to a NEW pod** (even a different machine, same region). So a spot reclaim → spin a fresh pod → mount the same volume → the loop resumes from the existing cache + `ckpt_latest`. Exactly what the design needs.

## The usual downside doesn't bite here
Network Volume is network-attached (slower than local NVMe), but this run is **GPU-compute-bound, not disk-bound**: the HF cache is read once at load, checkpoints are small writes every 250 steps, the teacher cache is written once. A few extra seconds on save/load is negligible vs the training. So you pay ~nothing for the persistence.

## Concrete
- **Network Volume, ~100 GB**, in the **same datacenter region** as the RTX PRO 6000 (the pod must match the volume's region).
- It holds both `HF_HOME=/workspace/hf` (Granite ~12 GB + HotpotQA → no re-download on a new pod) and `CKPT_DIR=/workspace/ckpt` (the teacher cache ~8 GB at 20k rows + checkpoints). 100 GB is comfortable (~35 GB used).

## When a plain Pod Volume Disk would be fine
Only if you run **on-demand** (not spot), never terminate the pod, and don't need portability — then the local disk is faster and simpler. But for a make-or-break run where losing the teacher cache means re-paying the biggest cost, the Network Volume's persistence wins. **Go Network Volume.**

(One caveat to check at create time: pick a region that actually has RTX PRO 6000 availability, since the volume pins you to that region.)

### 🟦 [2026-06-17 14:45:40] 操作者

SSH key not configured 要吗

### ⬜ [2026-06-17 14:46:19] Claude

**不是必须的,但建议配。** 关键不在 SSH 本身,而在别让长跑因为掉线而死。

## 不配也能跑
RunPod 控制台的 **Web Terminal**(浏览器里的 shell)能做全套:clone、`runpod_setup.sh`、`runpod_distill.sh`、`tail` 日志、`cat` 那几个 JSON。SSH key 不是跑通的前提。

## 但为什么建议配
这是个**长跑**(P0 ~30min–1.5h,scale 几小时)。两个实际好处:
1. **掉线不丢跑** —— 配合 SSH 开个 **tmux**,浏览器刷新/网络抖动不会杀掉进程。
2. **拉产物** —— 用 `scp`/`rsync` 把 `verdict.json` / `eval_card.json` / `train.log` 拉回你 Mac 再发我,比从网页终端复制干净(小 JSON 复制也行)。

## ⚠️ 真正必做的(不管用不用 SSH)
**在 tmux/screen 里启动 `runpod_distill.sh`**,否则启动它的那个 shell 一断,整个 self-heal 循环就停了(循环能自愈崩溃/抢占,但救不了"启动它的 shell 被杀")。
```
tmux new -s distill
# 在 tmux 里:bash scripts/runpod_distill.sh
# 断开:Ctrl-b d   重连:tmux attach -t distill
```

## 配 key(2 分钟)
本机有就直接用,没有就 `ssh-keygen -t ed25519`,把**公钥** `~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub` 内容贴到 RunPod → Settings → SSH Public Keys。然后用 pod 页面给的命令连(直连 `ssh root@<ip> -p <port>`,或 RunPod 代理那条)。

**一句话**:能不配就用 Web Terminal + tmux 直接开跑;想省事+方便拉产物就花 2 分钟配上。无论哪种,**tmux 是必须的**。

## 学到的 5 件事 → CF 怎么调

**① `KD_ANSWER_W=2.0` 这个"优化"杠杆其实在帮倒忙。** 它给**答案span的KD加倍权重**——而答案span正是Granite背下来的那个答案。等于在加倍蒸馏"复现记忆答案"=**强化鹦鹉**。→ CF run 用回 `1.0`(默认就是,不设它即可)。这是个反直觉的发现:上一轮的优化里有一项在反向拉。

**② best-ckpt 选择(`select_score`)也对 slope 失明** —— 跟 verdict 当初一样的毛病。slope≈0 时它退化成"只挑 E1 最低的",CF run 里就会挑**最后那个最流畅、但可能已经 nonce 崩坏**的 ckpt,而不是最会读的。→ **已修(add.53)**:CF run 用 `cf_lift`(因果阅读信号)选 best ckpt,不用瞎的 slope。已加测试,通过。

**③ 教师缓存可以复用,省 ~15–20 分钟。** CF run 的 config(N_ROWS=20000、P=0.8、K=4、teacher 全一样,CF步本身不进缓存)→ 指纹一致。启动 CF 前把 `/workspace/ckpt-opt/cache` + `eval_set.pt` 拷到 `ckpt-cf` 即可跳过重建缓存。

**④ 流畅度没饱和** → CF 可以边强制阅读边继续涨流畅度,不冲突。

**⑤ 运行很干净**(无发散/无 OOM/无非有限)→ CF 的 35% 纯CE步风险低。

(另注:`NOGOLD_CE=0` 但 20% 无金标样本仍吃 KD,而教师对它们也从记忆作答 → 一个**次要的鹦鹉通道**。第一次 CF run 先不动它,一次只上一个主干预。)

## 要训多久 —— 阶梯式,不要猜要测

| 阶段 | 步数 | ~token | 墙钟@3700tok/s | 目的 |
|---|---|---|---|---|

四个角度一致:**瓶颈是 token/优化量,不是容量**。证据——20k 那轮 E1 nll 到头还在降、EM=0、跟老师只 21% 一致,这是**喂不够**的特征,不是"模型表达不了"的天花板。**size 放到 2GB 反而证明 size 根本不是约束**:当前 544M 的 int8 才 **0.54GB**,离 2GB 远得很。所以 Run-1 把 10 小时全砸在修三个"饿":数据、优化步数、被浪费的后半程 LR——**容量一点不碰**。

## Run-1:≤10h 质量run(具体配方)

| 项 | 20k 旧值 | Run-1 | 为什么 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 模型 | 24L/544M | **24L/544M 不变** | 没到容量墙,先喂饱 |
| 步数 | 20k | **120k**(非130k) | ⚠️**对抗审查抓到的 bug**:130k 是"纯训练"正好10.0h,eval(每次5个条件×全长前向+CF生成)还要再加 0.7-7h→**会超10h**。降到120k + `EVAL_EVERY=2500` 才真装得下 |
| 优化更新 | 2.5k | **15k**(6×) | 这是 EM=0 的直接病因 |
| 数据 | 20k行(6.5轮) | **45k行**(2.9轮) | 减少过拟合,KD 多过几遍 |
| LR 调度 | cosine→2e-5(后半废) | **WSD**(warmup→**峰值平台**→末20%才衰减) | 旧 cosine 有48%的步跑在半峰以下;WSD **有效LR高1.7×** |
| WARMUP | 800 | 2000 | 按更新数(12%)而非原始步 |
| KD | top-64 renorm | **+KD_EXACT_TAIL=1** | logZ 已缓存→**零额外成本**,堵掉~1%的renorm偏差 |
| CF 阅读力 | — | **CF_FRAC=0.35 全程保持** | 这才是治 EM=0/鹦鹉的;且**衰减期不能撤CF**(会复发) |
| 出货 | — | **ckpt_best**(按cf_lift选) | 防止停在未衰减的ckpt |

**两个前置代码已实现+测试通过(add.55):**
- ✅ `DECAY=wsd` 分支(lr_at + 单测)—— 之前只有 cosine/linear/none,不加这个 `DECAY=wsd` 会**静默退回 cosine**,白白丢掉最大的那个杠杆。
- ✅ **in-loop 时间墙**(`MAX_SEC` 真正在训练循环里 save+break)—— 审查发现旧 `MAX_SEC` 只在崩溃重启间检查、健康run 完全无视它。

## 真正的最高杠杆:吞吐(决定 Run-2 能走多远)
审查纠正了一个关键点:**"97% GPU利用率"是指令发射占满,不是算力占满——实测 MFU 只有 3-6%,所以有 10-30× 余量,4-8× 提速是可信的**。
- **Stage A(低风险,1-2天)**:grad-checkpoint + 真正的 batch 维(**不是 vmap**——vmap 保留整条链才 OOM)+ torch.compile → **B=8,~3-4×**。必须重过 scan-parity 门。
- 这把 10h 从 13万步变成 ~4-5亿 token(3-4×)甚至 ~9-10亿(7-8×)。**Run-1 不等它,B=1 先跑;吞吐track 并行做。**

## 什么时候才放大模型(Run-2,双重门)
**只有**(rewrite 落地)**且**(Run-1 出现容量平台:nll 平了但 EM 还差)才放大 → 24L/D1280/741M(更稳,~50 tok/s)或 30L/D1280/895M(~42 tok/s,A19解码要先实测一个 D=1280 的点)。**封顶 ~1B/32L**(再深 ANE 段拒绝暴涨)。**nll 还在降时绝不先放大。**

## 诚实的预期 + 决策规则
- **预期**:Run-1 大概率把 E1 nll 压到远低于 6.25、把 EM 从 0 顶起来(高信心**超基线**;**中等信心**到"可用EM/F1"——残余不确定是:CF 到底教没教会读 + WSD 的 LR-面积收益是否真转化为收敛)。
- **跑完读曲线定下一步**:nll 还在降→**token-bound,做rewrite**(不是加参数);nll 平了+EM差→**第一个容量信号**→考虑放大;nll 见底回升→过拟合→停/加数据。

- **没读** → 先迭代 CF recipe,Run-1 暂缓(砸10h喂一个还在鹦鹉的模型是浪费)。

- **"2 GB then quantize"** → that *is* the standard path: a ~1B model is **2 GB fp16 → int8 → ~1 GB**. For headroom under 1 GB (or to push past 1B params), **int4** (e.g. 1.5B int4 = 0.75 GB).

So the refined rule: **on-device int8 < 1 GB → ~1B param ceiling** (down from the ~2B the old ≤2GB-int8 allowed). This actually *confirms* the research's modest-growth direction (741–895M) and just caps the top tighter.

**One honesty flag:** int8 is **quant-safe** for this arch (the convertibility memory: Mamba-3 converts as cleanly as Mamba-2). **int4 is not yet validated** — the quant-fidelity gate is still a stub. So if a future model needs int4 to fit <1GB, that gate must be measured first. Recommendation: stay on the **int8 path, ≤~895M–1B params** (0.9–1.0 GB) — no int4 risk, fits <1GB.
